source.title: CoReS: Compatible Representations via Stationarity
source.authors: Niccoló Biondi; F. Pernici; Matteo Bruni; A. Bimbo

record.tranche_reason: Tests direct cross-model compatibility in visual search using verification, retrieval and re-identification performance, rather than measuring representational distance similarity.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates whether features from upgraded vision models can be compared directly with older gallery features. It does not measure similarity between model-induced distances on shared inputs. The cited results from other work are not recorded as rows. Detailed values in several compatibility-matrix figures are figure-only; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: CoReS is a training method that builds old/new feature compatibility on purpose, using a fixed d-Simplex classifier. Nearly every result scores the authors' own method against other compatibility-training methods (BCT, ℓ2, IFT, LwF). No version is tested. V4 is about mapping one model's representations onto another's, often by a fitted (e.g. linear) map, and no map is fitted here. The only independently trained baseline (ITM/'Standard') is compared directly, with no map, and is incompatible. That is expected even under V4. The paper cites the Convergent Learning original (same subspaces, different bases) only as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially right. CoReS uses fixed d-Simplex classifier stationarity to learn compatible features without mappings or pairwise training. The authors report that it beats BCT, especially over multiple upgrades, and stays compatible when the architecture is upgraded.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a fixed d-Simplex classifier and reserved class regions to train stationary features for direct cross-model visual-search compatibility; it does not test the original sources' distance-geometry convergence measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Compatibility varies with the number of upgrade steps and model initialization; pre-training and Model Selection improve reported compatibility, while alphabetical versus random class ordering has little effect. The architecture comparison reports higher compatibility with increased expressive power, though detailed values are figure-only.

fits_no_version.finding: Independently trained models' features cannot be compared directly without a map. ITM: cross-test 0.12 against self-test 0.60 on CIFAR (Table 1). Standard/ITM: AC 0 on Market1501 and CASIA, with cross-tests near 0.5 against self-tests near 0.9 (Fig. 9a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained models' feature spaces are not directly interchangeable (identity map) without alignment or compatibility training.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: Evidence is task-level compatibility on visual-search benchmarks, not a direct measurement of representational alignment or distance-geometry similarity. Some multi-upgrade architecture results are presented only in figures, and several reported compatibility values are incomplete.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed cells from Table 2 are omitted because the flattened table layout does not support unambiguous assignment of every value to a comparison pair. Figure-only matrix entries and detailed cells from Figures 5-7, 9-10, 12-14, and the epoch sweep in Figure 11 are also omitted; relevant textual summaries and key aggregate results are retained.

untested.parts: No convergence of independently trained models with scale; the architecture ablation uses compatibility-trained models only.
No measure of shared features or subspaces across seeds; initialization runs all use compatibility training.
No linear or other map, stitching or relative representations is fitted between independently trained models.
No measure of the degree or causes of alignment.

missing.what: ITM compatibility matrix on CASIA/LFW with four upgrades. Cross-tests are about 0.50-0.54 against self-tests of 0.90-0.96, and the text says baselines score AC 0 in all scenarios.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' for V4 is rejected. Compatibility here is induced by training, and V4's mapping-based interchangeability is never tested. The paper states that independently initialized networks learn the same subspaces with different bases, citing the Convergent Learning original. It uses that statement as a premise, not as its own result.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test convergence of independently trained models' representations as model scale or capability increases.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representation alignment.
Does not measure shared features or subspaces across independently initialized models; initialization experiments measure task-level compatibility instead.
Tests direct cross-model visual-search compatibility without a learned mapping. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or compatibility without paired training data.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits are compared.
Uses different datasets and task metrics, but does not systematically compare similarity measures, their settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs as causes of convergence.
Reports incomplete task-level compatibility in some settings but does not measure representational alignment or test whether shared data or objectives explain it.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Single-upgrade verification, retrieval and re-identification settings, plus Market1501 two-upgrade CoReS
reader_labels.reason: CoReS meets the reported compatibility criterion in these settings, including direct comparison of upgraded query features with old gallery features (r6, r7, r14, r15, r17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Longer sequential upgrading and initialization variations
reader_labels.reason: Compatibility is incomplete in some conditions: CoReS misses a pair in the two-upgrade CIFAR experiment, has AC below 1 in longer CIFAR/face sequences, and AC changes with initialization (r19, r21, r32, r33, r34).
